mainTopic: Stories and דרשות about the three kings with no share in עולם הבא (ירבעם, אחאב, מנשה): רב אשי's dream, the wickedness and merits of אחאב, and the argument about מנשה.
overview: This amud finishes the story of רבי אבהו, who went back to teaching about the sins of the three wicked kings once he got better. It then tells how רב אשי called those kings 'our colleagues,' and מנשה came to him in a dream. מנשה tested him on where to start cutting bread for המוציא and taught him the answer. He then explained that the pull of עבודה זרה in his time was overwhelming, so רב אשי began calling the kings 'our teachers.' Next the גמרא turns to אחאב: what his name hints at, how his sins went beyond ירבעם's, and the פסוק showing he has no share in עולם הבא. It also explains the merits that earned kingship for עמרי and twenty-two years for אחאב, proving that אחאב protected a ספר תורה. רב נחמן says אחאב was 'balanced,' and רבי יוסף explains that his support of תלמידי חכמים wiped away half his sins. The amud closes with מנשה: the meaning of his name, the source that he has no share in עולם הבא, and רבי יהודה's view that his תשובה earned him one. רבי יוחנן says both sides read the same פסוק, and the second reading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אבהו recovers and teaches about the kings again
steps.stepSummary: After recovering from his illness, רבי אבהו went back to teaching about the three wicked kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he recovered, he went back and taught about them again.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי אבהו continues from before. He had promised during his illness to stop teaching about the three kings, but now that he is healthy he teaches about them again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אבהו became sick and took on himself not to give דרשות about the sins of the three kings. This line reports that once he got better, he went back to doing exactly that. This sets up his students' question in the next step.

phrases.english: When he recovered, he went back and lectured.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי אבהו from the story just before, and his lecture was about the three kings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי אבהו story from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו resumed teaching about the sins of the three kings after he recovered.

steps.title: The students question why he broke his promise
steps.stepSummary: The students challenge רבי אבהו: didn't you promise not to teach about them?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Didn't you take on yourself not to lecture about them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו's students point out that he seems to be going back on the commitment he made while sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about consistency. He accepted a commitment, and now he seems to be ignoring it. Breaking a commitment like that is a serious matter.

keyTerms.meaning: You took upon yourself / you committed

phrases.english: They said: Did you not take upon yourself
that you would not lecture about them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבי אבהו did in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's going back to lecturing about the kings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He had promised not to, so lecturing seems to break his word.

steps.title: They did not repent, so neither will I
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers: did the kings do תשובה, that I should change my mind about them?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Did they turn back from their ways, that I should turn back from mine?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends himself. Since the kings never repented, there is no reason for him to stop describing their sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is a parallel. If the kings had changed, it would be fitting to stop criticizing them. Since they did not change, his criticism still stands, and his promise made while sick does not hold him back.

keyTerms.meaning: I should retract / change my mind

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו kept teaching about the kings' sins because they never did תשובה.

phrases.english: He said: Did they turn back from their ways,
that I should turn back from mine?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ מִי הֲדַרוּ בְּהוּ, דַּאֲנָא אֶהְדַּר בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He should keep his promise not to lecture about them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since they never repented, there is no reason to hold back from teaching about their sins.

steps.title: רב אשי calls the kings 'our colleagues'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי stopped his lecture right before the topic of the three kings and said that tomorrow they would start with 'our colleagues.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי stopped at the topic of the three kings. He said: Tomorrow we will begin with our colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רב אשי casually calls the wicked kings his 'colleagues,' and this sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These kings were great Torah scholars, so רב אשי treated them as his equals. The word 'colleagues' is what triggers מנשה's anger in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The three kings who have no share in עולם הבא: ירבעם, אחאב, מנשה

phrases.english: Rav Ashi stopped at the three kings.
phrases.notes: His lecture ended right as it reached the topic of the three kings.

phrases.english: He said: Tomorrow we will begin with our colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story on the same topic of the three kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי referred to the three kings as 'our colleagues.'

steps.title: מנשה objects in a dream
steps.stepSummary: מנשה appears to רב אשי in a dream and protests being called his colleague.
steps.simpleTranslation: מנשה came and appeared to him in his dream. He said: You call us your colleagues, and your father's colleagues?
steps.whatsHappening: מנשה challenges רב אשי for treating the kings as his equals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנשה claims that he is far above רב אשי, and even above רב אשי's father, so calling him a 'colleague' is disrespectful. This sets up a test of who knows more.

phrases.english: Manasseh came,
and appeared to him in his dream.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: חֲבֵרָךְ וַחֲבֵירֵי דַּאֲבוּךְ קָרֵית לַן?
phrases.english: He said: You call us your colleagues, and the colleagues of your father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the word 'colleagues' from step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The kings were far greater in Torah than רב אשי, so calling them equals belittles them.

steps.title: מנשה tests רב אשי about ברכת המוציא
steps.stepSummary: מנשה asks from which part of the bread one should begin cutting when saying המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are you supposed to start cutting the bread for המוציא?
steps.whatsHappening: מנשה tests רב אשי with a practical הלכה question to show who knows more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of only claiming he is greater, מנשה gives proof by asking a basic practical question. If רב אשי cannot answer it, the claim that they are 'colleagues' falls apart.

phrases.english: From where must you begin for HaMotzi?
phrases.notes: He is asking which part of the loaf you should start cutting when you make the ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up מנשה's objection with a test.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where on the loaf to begin cutting when reciting המוציא

steps.title: רב אשי admits he does not know
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says: I don't know.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי honestly admits he does not know the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By admitting this, רב אשי shows that מנשה knew something he did not. This gives מנשה the opening for his rebuke in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the test question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי does not know the answer.

steps.title: מנשה's rebuke
steps.stepSummary: מנשה says: You don't even know this basic rule, and you call us your colleagues?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have not learned from where to begin cutting for המוציא, and you call us your colleagues?
steps.whatsHappening: מנשה uses רב אשי's admission to drive his point home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the objection from step 5, but now it has proof behind it. If רב אשי does not know a basic practical rule, he cannot claim to be on the kings' level.

phrases.english: He said to him: From where you must
begin for HaMotzi you have not learned,
and you call us your colleagues?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב אשי's admission to strengthen the challenge from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the kings are his equals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He does not know a basic rule, so he is not their equal.

steps.title: רב אשי asks to be taught
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks מנשה to teach him the rule and promises to quote it in מנשה's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Teach it to me, and tomorrow I will teach it in your name in my public lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי humbly asks מנשה to teach him the answer and offers to give him credit publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב אשי accepts the role of a student. Promising to say it in מנשה's name shows real respect for him as a source of Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Public lecture given on a יום טוב or שבת

phrases.english: He said to him: Teach it to me,
and tomorrow I will lecture it
in your name at the public lecture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the rebuke by asking to learn.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The answer to the המוציא question

steps.title: Begin cutting where the bread is best baked
steps.stepSummary: מנשה answers: begin from the place where the crust is most baked.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From the place where the baking has formed a crust.
steps.whatsHappening: מנשה gives the הלכה: when saying המוציא, start cutting at the well-baked, crusty part of the loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from step 6. It is a real practical rule, and it shows that מנשה truly was a master of Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: For המוציא, one begins cutting at the part of the loaf that is best baked and crusty.

phrases.english: He said to him: From where the baking has formed a crust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's request.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begin cutting from the crusty, well-baked part of the loaf.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a practical halacha about how to cut bread for המוציא.

steps.title: Why did someone so wise worship idols?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: if you were so wise, why did you serve עבודה זרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since you were so wise, why did you all worship idols?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב אשי asks מנשה a hard question: how could such a great scholar fall into idol worship?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנשה's wisdom, just shown in the previous step, makes his sin harder to understand. This sets up מנשה's explanation.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵאַחַר דְּחַכִּימַתְּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Since you are so wise,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא קָא פָּלְחִיתוּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason you worshipped idols?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאַחַר דְּחַכִּימַתְּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי, מַאי טַעְמָא קָא פָּלְחִיתוּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wisdom מנשה just showed to raise a contradiction.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person so wise should not have fallen into such a sin.

steps.title: You would have run after me
steps.stepSummary: מנשה answers: if you had lived then, you would have lifted your cloak and run after me to worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Had you been there, you would have lifted the hem of your cloak and run after me.
steps.whatsHappening: מנשה explains that the pull toward עבודה זרה in his time was so strong that even רב אשי would have given in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנשה does not deny the sin. He explains that the desire for idol worship back then was overwhelming, far beyond anything רב אשי experiences. So רב אשי should not judge them as if they lived in his world.
steps.confusionAlert: מנשה is not saying idol worship was allowed. He is saying the temptation was so strong in his time that it is hard for later people to understand.

phrases.english: He said to him: Had you been there,
you would have held up the hem of your cloak
phrases.notes: Like someone hitching up a long robe so he can run faster.

phrases.english: and run after me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wise person would never worship idols.
steps.terutzMaskana: The temptation in that time was so great that even a great scholar would have been drawn after it.

steps.title: רב אשי now calls them 'our teachers'
steps.stepSummary: The next day רב אשי told the חכמים: we will begin with our teachers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day he said to the Sages: We will begin with our teachers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי changes how he speaks about the kings. Instead of 'our colleagues,' he now calls them 'our teachers.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the story. רב אשי learned from the dream that the kings were greater than him in Torah, even though they sinned, and he corrects his wording from step 4.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי went from calling the kings 'colleagues' to calling them 'teachers.' Their sins did not erase their greatness in Torah.

phrases.english: The next day he said to the Sages:
We will begin with our teachers.
phrases.notes: Compare step 4, where he had said 'our colleagues.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רב אשי took the lesson of the dream to heart.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three kings, though sinners, were greater Torah scholars than later generations and should be spoken of as 'our teachers.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches respect for Torah greatness, even when it belongs to people who sinned badly.

steps.title: The meaning of the name אחאב
steps.stepSummary: The name אחאב is read as אח (brother) and אב (father): a brother to Heaven, a father to עבודה זרה. Each half is backed by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחאב's name means: a 'brother' to Heaven and a 'father' to idol worship. 'Brother to Heaven' comes from 'A brother is born for trouble.' 'Father to idol worship' comes from 'As a father has compassion on his children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing אחאב, the next king from the משנה, by splitting his name into two words that describe him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother is someone you turn to only in hard times, so אחאב turned to Heaven only when he was in trouble. A father loves his children deeply, so אחאב's attachment to עבודה זרה was full and loving. The contrast shows that his real devotion went to idols.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother to Heaven, close only in times of trouble
A father to idol worship, fully and lovingly devoted

phrases.english: Ahab: a brother to Heaven,
phrases.notes: The name אחאב is being split into two words, אח (brother) and אב (father).

phrases.english: a father to idol worship.
'A brother to Heaven,' as it is written:
'A brother is born for trouble.'
phrases.notes: משלי 17:17

phrases.english: 'A father to idol worship,' as it is written:
'As a father has compassion on his children.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 103:13

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחְאָב: אָח לַשָּׁמַיִם, אָב לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of מנשה to the next king in the משנה, אחאב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחאב's name shows he turned to Heaven only in trouble but loved עבודה זרה like a father loves his children.

steps.title: אחאב's light sins equal ירבעם's severe sins
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'the lightest thing was his walking in the sins of ירבעם,' רבי יוחנן teaches that אחאב's light sins were equal to ירבעם's severe ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The lightest thing was his walking in the sins of ירבעם בן נבט.' רבי יוחנן said: The light sins אחאב did were like the severe sins ירבעם did.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reads a פסוק about אחאב to show how much worse he was than ירבעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls following ירבעם's sins 'light' for אחאב. רבי יוחנן reads this exactly: what counted as small for אחאב was as big as ירבעם's biggest sins. So אחאב went far beyond ירבעם.

keyTerms.meaning: The light thing, the least of it
ירבעם בן נבט, the first king of the northern kingdom

phrases.english: 'And it was, the lightest thing was his walking'
'in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 16:31

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The light sins that Ahab did
were like the severe sins that Jeroboam did.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קַלּוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה אַחְאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing אחאב's wickedness, now by comparing him to ירבעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחאב's minor sins were as serious as ירבעם's major sins.

steps.title: Why does the verse blame ירבעם?
steps.stepSummary: If אחאב was worse, why does the פסוק still describe the sins as 'the sins of ירבעם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason did the פסוק attach the sins to ירבעם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that comes out of רבי יוחנן's teaching. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אחאב sinned far more, it seems strange that the פסוק names the sins after ירבעם. The question asks why ירבעם gets the label.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse attached or blamed it

phrases.english: And for what reason
did the verse attach it to Jeroboam?
phrases.notes: Literally 'hang it on' ירבעם. He means: name the sins after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a question that follows from רבי יוחנן's statement that אחאב was worse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק names the sins after ירבעם if אחאב's sins were greater.

steps.title: ירבעם started the corruption
steps.stepSummary: The sins are named after ירבעם because he was the first to begin the corruption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he was the first to start the corruption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: ירבעם is blamed because he started it all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though later kings like אחאב sinned more, ירבעם opened the path. The one who begins the damage carries the name of it.
steps.whatToRemember: The one who starts a bad path is held responsible for it, even when others later go further.

phrases.english: Because he was
the first to the corruption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירבעם is named because he was the first to bring in the corruption.

steps.title: אחאב placed idols on every furrow
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'their altars are like heaps on the furrows of the field,' רבי יוחנן says there was no furrow in ארץ ישראל where אחאב did not set up an idol and bow to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Also their altars are like heaps on the furrows of the field.' רבי יוחנן said: There is no furrow at all in ארץ ישראל on which אחאב did not set up an idol and bow down to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן uses another פסוק to show how widely אחאב spread עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the altars to heaps on every furrow of a field. רבי יוחנן applies it to אחאב: he set up idols everywhere in the land, on every single furrow. This adds a new detail: how far his idol worship reached.

keyTerms.meaning: A furrow in a plowed field

phrases.english: 'Also their altars are like heaps'
'on the furrows of the field.'
phrases.notes: הושע 12:12

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
You do not have any furrow at all
in the Land of Israel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱמִיד עָלָיו אַחְאָב עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: on which Ahab did not set up an idol
and bow down to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין לָךְ כׇּל תֶּלֶם וָתֶלֶם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching of רבי יוחנן about how great אחאב's idol worship was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחאב set up idols and bowed to them on every furrow in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Source that אחאב has no share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that אחאב does not enter עולם הבא, as the משנה stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he does not come to the World to Come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a פסוק that proves the משנה's claim that אחאב has no share in עולם הבא. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא described how wicked אחאב was. Now it asks for actual proof from a פסוק that he loses עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that he does not come to the World to Come?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא לַן דְּלָא אָתֵי לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from describing אחאב's sins to finding a source for his punishment stated in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that אחאב has no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Shut up in this world, abandoned in the next
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says God will cut off from אחאב the 'shut up' and the 'abandoned.' 'Shut up' refers to this world, 'abandoned' to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And I will cut off from אחאב every male, and the shut up and the abandoned in Israel.' 'Shut up' means in this world, and 'abandoned' means in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and reads its two words as two different punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two similar words, עצור and עזוב. The גמרא treats each as its own message: one is about this world, and the other is about עולם הבא. So the פסוק itself says אחאב is cut off from עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for אחאב losing עולם הבא is the word 'ועזוב' in the פסוק of his punishment.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And I will cut off from Ahab every male'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 21:21. Literally 'one who urinates against a wall,' a blunt way of saying every male.

phrases.english: 'and the shut up and the abandoned in Israel.'
'Shut up' means in this world,
'and abandoned' means in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'ועזוב' in the פסוק shows אחאב is cut off from עולם הבא, while 'עצור' refers to this world.

steps.title: Why עמרי merited kingship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks and answers: עמרי, אחאב's father, earned the kingship because he added a large city, שמרון, to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why did עמרי merit kingship? Because he added one large city in ארץ ישראל, as it says: 'And he bought the hill of שומרון from שמר for two talents of silver, and he built on the hill, and he called the name of the city that he built after שמר, the owner of the hill, שומרון.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains what good deed earned עמרי the throne, and he proves it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a wicked king can be rewarded for a real good deed. עמרי bought a hill and built a city there, adding to ארץ ישראל, and for this he earned kingship. The פסוק shows he bought, built, and named the city שמרון.

keyTerms.meaning: עמרי, king of Israel and father of אחאב

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea that God rewards a good deed even for someone who did much evil.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For what reason did Omri merit kingship?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוֹסִיף כְּרַךְ אֶחָד בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: Because he added one large city in the Land of Israel,
as it is said: 'And he bought the hill of Samaria'
'from Shemer for two talents of silver,'
'and he built on the hill,'
'and he called the name of the city that he built'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁם שֶׁמֶר אֲדֹנֵי הָהָר שֹׁמְרוֹן״.
phrases.english: 'after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill, Samaria.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 16:24

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכָה עׇמְרִי לַמַּלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אחאב himself to his father עמרי and the merit that brought his family to the throne.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמרי earned kingship because he added the city of שמרון to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: אחאב ruled 22 years for honoring the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אחאב earned twenty-two years of kingship because he honored the תורה, which is written with twenty-two letters. He brings the פסוקים about בן הדד's demands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why did אחאב earn twenty-two years as king? Because he honored the תורה, which is written with twenty-two letters. The פסוקים tell the story. בן הדד demanded אחאב's silver, gold, wives and children, and then threatened to take 'whatever is the delight of your eyes.' אחאב answered: 'Everything you asked for at first I will do, but this thing I cannot do.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second 'why did he merit' teaching, this time about אחאב himself, and quotes the פסוקים that will serve as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twenty-two years match the twenty-two letters of the תורה, so the reward fits the merit measure for measure. The key detail in the פסוקים is that אחאב gave in on everything except the 'delight of your eyes.' The next step explains what that was.

keyTerms.meaning: king of ארם, who besieged אחאב

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For what reason did Ahab merit
the kingship for twenty-two years?
Because he honored the Torah,
which was given with twenty-two letters,
phrases.notes: The אלף־בית has twenty-two letters, so his years match the letters of the תורה.

phrases.english: as it says: "And he sent messengers to Ahab
phrases.notes: מלכים א 20:2-3

phrases.english: king of Israel, into the city.

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ כֹּה אָמַר בֶּן הֲדַד
phrases.english: And he said to him: So says Ben-Hadad:
Your silver and your gold are mine,
and your wives and your good children are mine."
"But at this time tomorrow
phrases.notes: מלכים א 20:6. The גמרא skips a few verses in between.

phrases.english: I will send my servants to you

phrases.aramaic: וְחִפְּשׂוּ אֶת בֵּיתְךָ וְאֵת בָּתֵּי עֲבָדֶיךָ
phrases.english: and they will search your house and the houses of your servants,
and whatever is the delight of your eyes
they will put in their hand and take."
"And he said to Ben-Hadad's messengers:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 20:9

phrases.english: Tell my master the king:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַחְתָּ אֶל עַבְדְּךָ בָרִאשׁוֹנָה אֶעֱשֶׂה
phrases.english: Everything you sent for to your servant at first, I will do,
but this thing I cannot do."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכָה אַחְאָב לַמַּלְכוּת עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's series of 'why did he merit kingship' teachings, moving from עמרי to his son אחאב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחאב earned twenty-two years of kingship because he honored the תורה, which has twenty-two letters.

steps.title: The 'delight of your eyes' is a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof: the 'delight of your eyes' that אחאב refused to give up must be a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'the delight of your eyes'? Isn't it a ספר תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly where in the פסוקים רבי יוחנן sees אחאב honoring the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב was willing to hand over his gold, wives and children, but drew the line at the 'delight of your eyes.' If that was a ספר תורה, then he valued the תורה above everything else, and that is his merit.

phrases.english: What is "the delight of your eyes"?
Is it not a Torah scroll?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the פסוקים quoted in step 22 prove that אחאב honored the תורה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that אחאב honored the תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אחאב's refusal to hand over 'the delight of your eyes,' understood as a ספר תורה.

steps.title: Maybe the treasured item was an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading: maybe the 'delight of your eyes' was an idol, which a wicked king like אחאב would treasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it was an idol?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by offering another way to read 'delight of your eyes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that אחאב was deeply involved in idol worship (step 18). So the thing he refused to give up might have been his idol, and then the story would show nothing about honoring the תורה.

phrases.english: Perhaps it was an idol?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 23 reading that 'delight of your eyes' means a ספר תורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The identification of 'the delight of your eyes' as a ספר תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Given אחאב's devotion to idols, the treasured item could just as easily have been an idol.

steps.title: The elders told him to refuse, so it was not an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idol reading: the elders advised אחאב to refuse בן הדד, and elders would not urge him to protect an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because it is written: 'And all the elders and all the people said to him: Do not agree and do not listen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ספר תורה reading by pointing to the elders who backed אחאב's refusal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'elders' are taken to be the חכמים. They would not tell the king to risk war to protect an idol. So the treasured item must have been something holy, the ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: it cannot enter your mind; that is impossible

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind,
for it is written: "And they said to him,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 20:8

phrases.english: all the elders and all the people:
phrases.notes: The גמרא takes 'elders' to mean the חכמים, who would never back protecting an idol.

phrases.english: Do not agree and do not listen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 24 challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from context: who gave the advice shows what was being protected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'delight of your eyes' might have been an idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: The elders (חכמים) backed the refusal, so it must have been a ספר תורה.

steps.title: Maybe they were wicked elders, like אבשלום's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe these 'elders' were wicked, like the 'elders of Israel' who supported אבשלום, whom רב יוסף calls shameful elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they were shameful elders? Isn't it written: 'And the plan pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel'? And רב יוסף said: those were shameful elders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 25 by showing that the word 'elders' does not always mean righteous חכמים. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 depended on the elders being righteous. But in the story of אבשלום, 'elders of Israel' supported a wicked plan against דוד, and רב יוסף says they were wicked. If the same could be true here, the elders might have been protecting an idol after all.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's son who rebelled against him

phrases.english: But perhaps they were shameful elders?
phrases.notes: Literally 'elders of shame,' meaning wicked elders.

phrases.english: Isn't it written:
"And the plan was right in the eyes of Absalom
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 17:4

phrases.english: and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel"?
And Rav Yosef said: those were shameful elders.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ספר תורה reading has been dropped. The גמרא answers this challenge in the next step.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 25 that the elders were righteous.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 25 assumption that 'elders' means righteous חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere in תנ״ך, 'elders of Israel' were wicked (רב יוסף on the אבשלום story), so the elders here might also have been wicked, and the idol reading comes back.

steps.title: All the people agreed, and some of them were surely righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from אבשלום's elders. In אחאב's story the פסוק adds 'and all the people,' and among all the people there must have been צדיקים. A פסוק confirms there were seven thousand faithful people in that generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the אבשלום story it does not say 'and all the people.' Here it does say 'and all the people,' and it is impossible that there were no righteous people among them. And it is written: 'I will leave in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that did not bow to the בעל and every mouth that did not kiss it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge. It points out that in אחאב's story, 'all the people' joined the elders, and that group surely included צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 26 was that the elders might have been wicked, like the elders who backed אבשלום. The difference is the extra phrase 'and all the people.' In אחאב's time there were seven thousand people who never served the בעל, so righteous people were part of the decision. They would not have backed protecting an idol, so the 'delight of your eyes' must have been a ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here: the גמרא compares two cases
The בעל, the main idol worshipped in אחאב's time

steps.whatToRemember: The proof holds: righteous people backed אחאב's refusal, so what he guarded was a ספר תורה, not an idol.

phrases.english: There it is not written "and all the people,"
phrases.notes: "There" means the אבשלום story from the last step. "Here" means אחאב's story with בן הדד.

phrases.english: here it is written "and all the people,"

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא הֲווֹ בְּהוֹן צַדִּיקֵי.
phrases.english: for it is impossible that there were no righteous people among them.
And it is written: "And I will leave in Israel seven thousand,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 19:18

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַבִּרְכַּיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא כָרְעוּ לַבַּעַל
phrases.english: all the knees that did not bow to the בעל

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַפֶּה אֲשֶׁר לֹא נָשַׁק לוֹ״.
phrases.english: and every mouth that did not kiss it."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא כְּתִיב וְכׇל הָעָם, הָכָא כְּתִיב וְכׇל הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by pointing to a wording difference between the two stories.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual distinction: the phrase 'and all the people' appears only in אחאב's story.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The elders who advised אחאב might have been wicked, like אבשלום's elders.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the people agreed, and that group included צדיקים, so the treasure was holy: a ספר תורה.

steps.title: אחאב was balanced between merits and sins
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says אחאב's merits and sins were equal. He proves it from the heavenly discussion where 'this one said this way and that one said that way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: אחאב was balanced, as it says: 'And ה׳ said, who will entice אחאב so he will go up and fall at רמות גלעד? And this one said this way, and that one said that way.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens. רב נחמן says אחאב was exactly half good and half bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In heaven, opinions about how to bring אחאב down were split. רב נחמן reads this split as a sign that his record was evenly balanced. This sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: רמות גלעד, the battlefield where אחאב died

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Ahab was balanced,
phrases.notes: He means half merits and half sins.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ מִי יְפַתֶּה אֶת אַחְאָב
phrases.english: as it says: "And ה׳ said, who will entice Ahab
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:20

phrases.english: so that he will go up and fall at Ramot Gilad?

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר זֶה בְּכֹה וְזֶה אֹמֵר בְּכֹה״.
phrases.english: And this one said this way, and that one said that way."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַחְאָב שָׁקוּל הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about אחאב: how his merits and sins balanced out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחאב's merits and sins were equal, as shown by the split opinions in heaven.

steps.title: How can the most wicked king be called balanced?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסף objects. The פסוק says no one sold himself to evil like אחאב, and a ברייתא says איזבל weighed out gold for idol worship every day. How can אחאב be called balanced?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסף objected: About this man it is written, 'There was none like אחאב, who sold himself to do evil in the eyes of ה׳, whom איזבל his wife incited.' And we learned in a ברייתא that every day she would weigh out gold shekels for idol worship. And you say he was balanced?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסף attacks רב נחמן's statement, using a פסוק and a ברייתא that show אחאב was extremely wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls אחאב worse than anyone. The ברייתא adds that his household spent gold on idol worship every single day. A record like that does not look anywhere close to half good.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosef objects to it:
The one about whom it is written:
"But there was none like Ahab,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 21:25

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הִתְמַכֵּר לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי ה׳
phrases.english: who sold himself to do evil in the eyes of ה׳,
whom Izevel his wife incited,"
and we learned:
every day she would weigh out
phrases.notes: "She" is איזבל.

phrases.english: gold shekels for idol worship,
and you say he was balanced?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's claim from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that אחאב was balanced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק and a ברייתא show that אחאב was extremely wicked, which does not fit a balanced record.

steps.title: His generosity to Torah scholars wiped away half his sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אחאב was generous with his money and supported תלמידי חכמים. Because of this, half his sins were forgiven, which left him balanced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אחאב was generous with his money, and because he let תלמידי חכמים benefit from his property, half his sins were forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסף keeps going with 'אֶלָּא' (rather) and gives a new way to understand רב נחמן's 'balanced': it explains how so wicked a man could still end up balanced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב really did commit huge sins. But supporting תלמידי חכמים earned him so much merit that half his sins were wiped away. After that, what remained came out even.
steps.whatToRemember: Supporting תלמידי חכמים carries enormous merit. It forgave half the sins of even אחאב.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not deny that אחאב was very wicked. It explains that his merit erased half his sins, and that is how he ended up balanced.

phrases.english: Rather, Ahab was generous with his money,
and because he let Torah scholars benefit from his property,
they atoned for him half.
phrases.notes: Half of his sins were wiped away, so what was left came out even.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following the objection in step 29, 'אֶלָּא' recasts רב נחמן's claim: אחאב was balanced only after half his sins were atoned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: 'balanced' describes his record after half his sins were forgiven.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Balanced' means he was never very wicked.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was very wicked, but his support of תלמידי חכמים erased half his sins, which left him balanced.

steps.title: Which spirit volunteered to mislead אחאב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים about a spirit that offered to become a lying spirit in the mouths of אחאב's prophets, and it asks which spirit this was.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the spirit came out and stood before ה׳ and said: I will entice him. ה׳ said: With what? He said: I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. He said: You will entice him and succeed; go out and do so.' What spirit was this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rest of the heavenly scene and asks who 'the spirit' was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the spirit,' as if it were a particular, known one. That wording invites the question of exactly which spirit it was.

phrases.english: "And the spirit came out and stood before ה׳,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:21–22

phrases.english: and said: I will entice him.
And ה׳ said to him: With what?
And he said: I will go out and be a lying spirit
in the mouth of all his prophets.
And He said: You will entice him and also succeed;
go out and do so."
What spirit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same heavenly scene quoted in step 28 and asks about its next detail.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of 'the spirit' in the פסוק.

steps.title: It was the spirit of נבות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the spirit was the spirit of נבות היזרעאלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It was the spirit of נבות היזרעאלי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן identifies the spirit as נבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבות was killed so that אחאב could take his vineyard. That explains why his spirit would volunteer to bring אחאב down.

keyTerms.meaning: נבות from יזרעאל, the man killed so אחאב could take his vineyard

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The spirit of Navot the Yizre'eli.
phrases.notes: נבות was killed so אחאב could take his vineyard (מלכים א 21).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רוּחוֹ שֶׁל נָבוֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.

steps.title: What does 'go out' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ה׳ meant when He told the spirit 'go out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'go out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the words 'go out.' This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spirit had already offered to go. So ה׳'s command 'go out' seems to say something extra, and the גמרא wants to know what it adds.

phrases.english: What is "go out"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about another word in the פסוק quoted in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'go out' in ה׳'s command.

steps.title: Go out from My presence, because liars cannot stand before ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that 'go out' means leave My presence for good, because ה׳ does not let speakers of lies stand before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It means 'go out from My presence,' for it is written: 'One who speaks lies shall not stand before My eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains that 'go out' was a banishment. Since the spirit chose to lie, it could no longer stay before ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mission did succeed, but the spirit paid a price for it. A פסוק in תהלים teaches that liars cannot stand in ה׳'s presence, so the spirit was sent out permanently.

keyTerms.meaning: My partition: My presence, My inner area

phrases.english: Ravina said:
"Go out from My presence,"
for so it is written:
"One who speaks lies shall not stand before My eyes."
phrases.notes: תהלים 101:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Go out' means a permanent banishment from ה׳'s presence, because liars cannot stand before Him.

steps.title: One who takes revenge destroys his own house
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא connects this to a popular saying: someone who takes revenge out of zealous anger ends up destroying his own home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: One who takes revenge out of his zealotry destroys his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא closes the section by tying נבות's story to a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבות's spirit got its revenge on אחאב. But the lie it used for that revenge cost it its own place before ה׳. Revenge hurt the one who took it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

steps.whatToRemember: Even a justified grievance, pursued as revenge through dishonest means, can destroy the person pursuing it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
One who takes revenge out of his zealotry destroys his own house.
phrases.notes: נבות's spirit got its revenge but lost its own place before ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up steps 32 and 34 with a folk saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking revenge out of zealotry ends up harming the avenger, as נבות's spirit was banished.

steps.title: What אחאב wrote on the doors of שומרון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains how אחאב angered ה׳ more than all the kings before him: he publicly wrote that he denied the God of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says אחאב made the אשרה and angered ה׳ more than all the kings of Israel before him. רבי יוחנן says this means he wrote on the doors of שומרון: 'אחאב denies the God of Israel, so he has no share in the God of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about אחאב, and רבי יוחנן explains what extra evil act made him worse than the kings before him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says אחאב 'did more' to anger ה׳, without saying what he did. רבי יוחנן fills this in: he openly announced his denial of ה׳ on the city gates for everyone to see. This adds to the picture of why אחאב has no share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree or pole that was worshipped as an idol
The doors (gates) of שומרון, the capital of the northern kingdom

phrases.english: "And Ahab made the ashera;
phrases.notes: מלכים א 16:33

phrases.english: and Ahab did more to provoke
the Lord, God of Israel, to anger

phrases.aramaic: מִכֹּל מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ לְפָנָיו״.
phrases.english: than all the kings of Israel that were before him."
Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
That he wrote on the doors of Samaria:
phrases.notes: He is explaining what the 'did more' in the פסוק was.

phrases.english: Ahab denies the God of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בֵּאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: therefore he has no share in the God of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁכָּתַב עַל דַּלְתוֹת שֹׁמְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of אחאב with another דרשה about his wickedness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחאב's extra provocation was publicly writing on the gates of שומרון that he denied the God of Israel.

steps.title: What אחזיה did while hiding in שומרון
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that while אחזיה was hiding in שומרון, he cut God's names out of holy writings and wrote names of idols in their place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says they looked for אחזיה and caught him while he was hiding in שומרון. רבי לוי says he was cutting out the names of God and writing idol names in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related comment about אחזיה, a king from אחאב's family, and רבי לוי explains what he was doing while hiding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word 'hiding,' and רבי לוי reads it as hiding to secretly do something terrible. Replacing God's name with idol names is a very deep insult to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Mentions of God's name in holy writings
Idol worship; here, the name of an idol

phrases.english: "And he sought Ahaziah,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 22:9

phrases.english: and they apprehended him, for he was hiding in Samaria."
Rabbi Levi says:
That he would cut out the mentions of God's name,
phrases.notes: He is explaining what אחזיה was busy doing while he hid.

phrases.english: and write idol worship in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֵר אַזְכָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related side comment about another king of אחאב's family who also sinned in שומרון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While hiding, אחזיה erased God's names and wrote idol names in their place.

steps.title: Two explanations of the name מנשה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to מנשה, the third king in the משנה, and gives two explanations of his name, both based on the idea of forgetting God.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was called מנשה because he forgot God. Another explanation: he was called מנשה because he made Israel forget their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to מנשה and starts, as it did with the other kings, by explaining what his name hints at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name מנשה sounds like the root נשה, 'to forget.' The first explanation says he himself forgot ה׳. The second says he caused the whole nation to forget ה׳, which is even worse.

phrases.english: Manasseh – because he forgot God.
phrases.notes: The name מנשה sounds like נשה, 'forgot.'

phrases.english: Another explanation:
Manasseh – because he caused Israel to forget
their Father Who is in Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the section on מנשה, the third king listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name מנשה hints at forgetting God, either himself forgetting or making Israel forget.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מנשה has no share in עולם הבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that מנשה does not enter עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we learn that he does not come to עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the משנה's claim that מנשה has no share in עולם הבא. The next step will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists מנשה among the kings with no share in עולם הבא, but it does not say where this comes from. The גמרא wants a פסוק to support it.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he does not come to the World-to-Come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the name, the גמרא asks for the source of מנשה's punishment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that מנשה has no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: מנשה is compared to אחאב
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says מנשה made an אשרה just like אחאב did, so just as אחאב has no share in עולם הבא, neither does מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'מנשה was twelve years old when he became king, and he ruled fifty-five years in Jerusalem... and he made an אשרה as אחאב king of Israel did.' Just as אחאב has no share in עולם הבא, so too מנשה has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to a פסוק that puts מנשה side by side with אחאב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we already know אחאב has no share in עולם הבא, the פסוק's comparison 'as אחאב did' carries over to מנשה. The proof works by linking the two kings.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה מְנַשֶּׁה בְמׇלְכוֹ
phrases.english: As it is written: "Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 21:1–3. The גמרא skips the middle and jumps to the part about the אשרה.

phrases.english: and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּעַשׂ אֲשֵׁרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אַחְאָב מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: and he made an ashera, as Ahab king of Israel did."

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַחְאָב אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: Just as Ahab has no share in the World-to-Come,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מְנַשֶּׁה אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: so too, Manasseh has no share in the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה מְנַשֶּׁה בְמׇלְכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares מנשה to אחאב, so he shares אחאב's fate of having no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: מנשה does have a share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה, who says מנשה does have a share in עולם הבא, because ה׳ accepted his prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: מנשה has a share in עולם הבא, as it says: 'And מנשה prayed to ה׳, and He accepted his prayer,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the opposing view from the משנה: רבי יהודה holds that מנשה does get a share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's proof is that ה׳ answered מנשה's prayer and brought him back to his kingdom. This shows that his תשובה was accepted, so he was not shut out of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on; the rest of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides: the תנא קמא of the משנה says מנשה has NO share, and רבי יהודה says he DOES have a share.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מְנַשֶּׁה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: Manasseh has a share in the World-to-Come,
as it is stated: "And Manasseh prayed to the Lord,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 33:13

phrases.english: and He was entreated of him, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says ה׳ heard him and brought him back to Jerusalem as king.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְנַשֶּׁה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to the one just proven in step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה holds that מנשה has a share in עולם הבא because ה׳ accepted his prayer.

steps.title: Both sides learn from the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה and the חכמים both base their views on one פסוק in ירמיהו that mentions מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from the same פסוק, as it says: 'And I will make them a horror for all the kingdoms of the earth, because of מנשה son of חזקיהו.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says the two sides in the argument are really reading the same פסוק in different ways. This sets up the next step, where each reading is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each side had its own proof. רבי יוחנן shows that the real argument is about how to understand the words 'because of מנשה' in one פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They interpreted one and the same פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
And both of them interpreted one verse,
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means רבי יהודה and the חכמים of the משנה.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And I will make them into a horror
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 15:4

phrases.english: for all the kingdoms of the earth,
on account of Manasseh, son of Hezekiah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the argument between steps 40 and 41 comes down to one shared פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions about מנשה are based on reading 'because of מנשה' in ירמיהו 15:4.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reading: מנשה did תשובה and they did not
steps.stepSummary: One side (רבי יהודה) reads 'because of מנשה' to mean the people are punished because even מנשה did תשובה and they didn't. The other side's reading begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: 'because of מנשה,' who did תשובה, while they did not. And the other Sage holds:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק and then starts the reading of the other side, which continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, מנשה is used as a measuring stick: if someone as wicked as he could do תשובה, the people have no excuse. This reading assumes מנשה's תשובה was real, which fits his view that מנשה has a share in עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: בִּגְלַל מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
phrases.english: One Sage holds: "On account of Manasseh," who repented,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's reading.

phrases.english: and they did not do so.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the people of Israel, who are punished for not following his example.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים' reading, and it continues right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: בִּגְלַל מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how one side reads the פסוק quoted in step 42, and begins the other side's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה reads 'because of מנשה' as: the people are judged harshly because מנשה repented and they did not.
